title: Type file (spec/fields/<entity_type>.json)
description: A type's whole definition (SPEC.md §4a, ADR-017, ADR-054): its kind, the ordered identity tiers SPEC.md §4 reads, the shared vocabulary per entity type, and the references its fields declare. A field name crossing an adapter boundary must appear here or be vendor-namespaced (<vendor>.<field>). Canonical names must not contain a dot; a dot marks a namespaced name. Types are discovered from the binary (person, company, post), from ~/.gtme/types/<name>.json, and from an installed binding's types/<name>.json in place; embedded names are reserved.

entity_type.description: The type's name — what a manifest's entity_type and a RECORD's key.entity_type say (SPEC.md §3). Must equal the file's basename.

version.description: Registry version. Additive changes do not bump it; renames (breaking) do.

kind.description: ADR-054: a subject (person, company) is what a pipeline delivers to; a signal (post) is what a pipeline finds and traverses from — keyed on a platform-public identifier, related to a subject, never the target of a deliver step. A signal declares no hash tier.

identity.description: The ordered key tiers SPEC.md §4 reads, strongest first: the runner takes the first tier that yields a value, and a record matching an existing identity under a weaker tier upgrades it in place. A field tier names a registry field in this file whose normalization is a public-identifier rule (email, domain, linkedin_url, handle, url); its key is that rule's key form (for linkedin_url, the path slug — SPEC.md §4). A hash tier is the nh: fallback: the components' normalized values, lowercased with whitespace collapsed, joined with '|' and sha256-hashed; the first component is required, later ones contribute their value or an empty string. A vendor's record id is never a tier.

field.description: A registry field in this file whose normalization is one of email, domain, linkedin_url, handle, url.

hash.description: The components of a name-hash tier, in order.

prefix.description: A literal key prefix (gh:, tw:, nh:), so tiers whose values could collide stay distinct in one identity_key column.

hashComponent.description: One component of a hash tier: a field name; {any: [...]} — the first alternative that yields a value; or {join: [...]} — the named fields' values joined with a space, present only when every one is.

reference.description: ADR-054: a record carrying this field also names an identity of `type`, keyed and populated from `fields` carried under the same names; the runner resolves-or-mints it and writes `relation` from the record to it. A referenced identity is a ledger fact, never a run member.

name.description: Canonical field name: lower_snake_case, no dots (dots mark vendor-namespaced names, which are never listed here).

tier.description: identity = backs key derivation (SPEC.md §4, mandatory set per ADR-017): the fields the identity list names; core = canonical shared vocabulary. The third tier (vendor namespace) is everything not in this file.

type.description: JSON type of the stored value.

items_type.description: Element type when type is array.

normalization.description: Named normalization rule (SPEC.md §4a); each id maps to exactly one implementation, shared with identity-key derivation. A stored canonical value must be a fixed point of its rule.

enum.description: Canonical value domain, where comparability matters (SPEC.md §4a tier 2).

reserved.description: Declared for tier ordering but provided by no v0 adapter (the ADR-020 handle tiers).

example.description: An example value in normalized form.
